CFML Language Reference: Functions

ParameterExists

Returns YES if the named variable exists. Unlike IsDefined, the variable name is written as is, without quotes.

Category

Decision functions

Syntax

ParameterExists(variable_name)

Parameters

variable_name
The variable name, not in quotes, optionally with a scope prefix, for example Form.Email.

Returns

YES or NO.

Usage

ParameterExists dates from the early days of the product and is kept so that old templates keep working. New code should use IsDefined, which takes the name as a string and so can test names built at run time. Because the argument is not evaluated, do not put quotes or pound signs around it.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Greeting = "Hello">
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Old style</TH><TH>Result</TH><TH>New style</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TR><TD><TT>ParameterExists(Greeting)</TT></TD><TD>#ParameterExists(Greeting)#</TD>
<TD><TT>IsDefined("Greeting")</TT></TD><TD>#IsDefined("Greeting")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD><TT>ParameterExists(URL.Color)</TT></TD><TD>#ParameterExists(URL.Color)#</TD>
<TD><TT>IsDefined("URL.Color")</TT></TD><TD>#IsDefined("URL.Color")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD><TT>ParameterExists(Form.Color)</TT></TD><TD>#ParameterExists(Form.Color)#</TD>
<TD><TT>IsDefined("Form.Color")</TT></TD><TD>#IsDefined("Form.Color")#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
